text:
Mikael Backlund is 37, has played 1,167 NHL games, every one of them for Calgary, and is still logging 18.4 minutes a night. The production says he is fading: 6 points in 19 games, none on the power play. The chances say something kinder.

He has 3 goals on 5.36 expected goals, the quality of the looks he has had, and his 5.8% shooting sits well under his usual range of 8.8% to 12.9%. Calgary has also scored 7.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. That is the profile of a player getting robbed more than a player slowing down, and our numbers flag him as due.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs it up: last season he set up 10.9 primary shot assists per 60, 97th percentile among forwards, and got to the home-plate area in front of the net often. Evolving-Hockey had his overall value near replacement level in 2025-26, but opponents got fewer chances with him out there. The 2022-23 King Clancy winner still does the hard parts. What we'd watch is whether the finish catches up with the work.
headline: Backlund is creating, and the puck is not cooperating
